newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ DEFU to project rebound in export growth - Smith.
newsitem.headline: NZ DEFU to project rebound in export growth - Smith.

text.p: The December economic and fiscal update to be released by the government on Monday would project a rebound in export growth from mid-1997 on current policy settings, Agriculture Minister Lockwood Smith said on Wednesday.
The six-monthly update would show a budget surplus little different from that projected before the general election, Smith told an annual conference of the Fruitgrowers' Federation in Wellington.
He said despite the strong New Zealand dollar, exports were still projected to grow by 4.3 percent a year from 1996 through to the turn of the century.
"Business profits have grown at a rate higher than expected, as has the economy at large," he said.
"It is remarkable that at the bottom of a business cycle we continue to have real growth of over two percent a year."

Smith said he was confident export conditions would not deteriorate so long as political parties negotiating the shape of the coalition government kept in mind that a strong economy provided a strong base for all businesses.
He told the federation that pipfruit exports this year had passed half a billion dollars, and exports of process fruit had reached a record NZ$145 million.
For kiwifruit, revenue and volume were ahead of the past two seasons, and the industry could be pleased with the export performance of both berries and sub-tropicals.
"Overall, fruit exports have remained about the same as last year," he said.
